key_highlights: ASX registers a third consecutive week of gains driven by broad-based rallies across mining and technology sectors.
Australian unemployment surges to a five-year high, triggering a sharp decline in AUD/USD and tempering RBA rate hike expectations despite persistent core inflation concerns.
Sydney property auction clearance rates deteriorate sharply, increasing scrutiny on major bank mortgage books.
Global trade risks escalate with 'China Shock 2.0' warnings, while domestic resource exploration momentum remains robust in gold, copper, rare earths, and lithium.

sectors.trend: Strong momentum in large-cap miners, junior gold explorers, rare earths, and major lithium expansion projects.
sectors.implications: Sustained capital flows into resource equities support ^AXJO, though China industrial overcapacity and export dynamics present medium-term demand risks.

sectors.trend: Rising macro headwinds as unemployment hits 5-year highs and auction clearance rates plunge in Sydney residential property.
sectors.implications: Asset quality, loan growth, and net interest margins for major banks face headwinds; credit impairment provisions may need upward revisions.

sectors.trend: Severe East Coast domestic gas supply tightening compounded by ongoing geopolitical supply disruptions in Europe.
sectors.implications: Elevated wholesale energy prices benefit domestic gas producers, but add structural cost pressures to energy-intensive manufacturers.

sectors.trend: Tech equities extend gains in tandem with resource stocks, buoyed by declining bond yields post-jobs data.
sectors.implications: Multiple expansion in ASX tech names supported by lower terminal cash rate expectations from the RBA.

sectors.trend: Pressured consumer discretionary spend, cruise capacity cuts, and governance investigations into retail leadership.
sectors.implications: Headwinds for discretionary retailers as softening labor market and real wage pressure curb household outlays.

key_themes: RBA Monetary Policy Divergence: Weakening labor market vs. sticky inflation dilemma.
China Shock 2.0: Chinese industrial overcapacity and deflationary export pressures.
Australian Housing Market Vulnerability: Auction weakness and rising debt service risks.
Commodity Exploration Surge: Gold and critical minerals securing defensive and growth capital.

risk_assessment.risk_factor: Labor Market Deterioration & Household Debt Stress
risk_assessment.mitigation: Underweight high-LVR exposed retail banking; rotate into defensive dividend payers and cash-rich mining majors.
Hedge exposure to trade-exposed manufacturing; favor producers of high-grade bulk commodities with cost-curve advantages.
Maintain floating rate debt exposure and high-quality liquid assets; hedge AUD/USD downside.
Overweight upstream gas suppliers with uncontracted East Coast volume capabilities.

opportunities.rationale: Strong commodity price backdrop, operational leverage, and active exploration pipelines offer resilient cash flows amid currency depreciation.

opportunities.recommendation: Selective Allocation to High-Quality ASX Technology
opportunities.rationale: Tech stocks are leading index gains and benefiting from falling local bond yield pressure following weak employment prints.

opportunities.recommendation: Capitalise on East Coast Gas Supply Deficit
opportunities.rationale: Tightening domestic gas dynamics support sustained elevated wholesale pricing and margin expansion for upstream producers.

defensive_moves.recommendation: Trim Exposure to Major Domestic Retail Banks
defensive_moves.rationale: Surging unemployment and housing auction weakness increase mortgage arrears risk and cap retail banking loan book expansion.

defensive_moves.recommendation: Underweight Consumer Discretionary & Retailers Facing Governance/Demand Headwinds
defensive_moves.rationale: Eroding consumer confidence, regulatory scrutiny, and corporate governance overhangs heighten downside risk.

defensive_moves.recommendation: Hedge ASX 200 Index Downside via Index Options or Inverse Exposures
defensive_moves.rationale: Three-week rally in ^AXJO may face resistance as macroeconomic fundamentals diverge from equity valuations.

market_outlook.short_term: ASX expected to trade range-bound (7,800–8,100 range) as resource and tech momentum battles deteriorating macroeconomic data and banking headwinds.
market_outlook.long_term: Cautiously optimistic on resource exporters and critical minerals; subdued outlook for domestic credit growth and consumer-facing cyclicals.
key_catalysts: Next RBA Cash Rate decision and quarterly Statement on Monetary Policy.
Q3 Australian CPI inflation print to confirm disinflation trajectory.
Global policy responses and tariff measures concerning Chinese industrial export surpluses.
East Coast domestic gas market regulatory interventions.
watch_list: AUD/USD exchange rate support levels around 0.6400-0.6500.
Sydney and Melbourne residential property auction clearance rates.
Australian monthly unemployment rate and labor underutilisation metrics.
Iron ore (SGX) and lithium carbonate benchmark pricing.
